Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Rivers (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE - joined 14:10), Sarah Patel (Velosys Head of ML), Jorge Martinez (Velosys CTO), Leah O'Connor (Velosys SRE), Tom Wu (Velosys FinOps)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and a practical cost breakdown. Customer wants to understand per-route cost allocation, alerting & quota controls, and data residency/security for a pilot.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the Velosys account, and with me is Ethan who's gonna walk through the console. Quick intros?
[00:10] Sarah: Hi this is Sarah, I head ML at Velosys. We're mainly evaluating how Redwood's runtime and console can help us ship an assistant across a few products.
[00:17] Jorge: Jorge, CTO. Focused on cost controls and ops surface.
[00:20] Leah: Leah, SRE — curious about alerts, quotas, VPC/private options.
[00:25] Tom: Tom, FinOps, mostly numbers and forecasting.
[00:28] Ethan: Great, thanks. I'll share my screen and jump into the Redwood Console. 
[00:35] [screen share noises - brief pause] 
[01:05] Ethan: Ok so top level view, this is the usage analytics page. You can see tokens/day, requests/min, and importantly per-route breakdowns. We often see teams create a route for each product surface — chat, summarization, embeddings, etc.
[01:22] Jorge: Quick question — when you say "per-route", is that per-API route or per logical route? How granular can we get?
[01:30] Ethan: Good question. It's logical routes you define in the console — you map each API endpoint or model configuration to a route name. We capture usage at the request and token level, so you can group by model, route, or tags.
[01:45] Sarah: And does that capture streaming tokens separately? For our assistant we stream a lot.
[01:50] Ethan: Yes, streaming and non-streaming tokens are both counted. We show latency-percentile charts alongside tokens to correlate cost vs latency.
[02:05] [02:05] Maya: Tom, I know you're focused on forecasting — Ethan will show the cost breakdown view.
[02:12] Ethan: Right, here's the per-route cost breakdown. We compute cost using your pricing profile — per-token generation and per-token input cost — plus model-specific multipliers for larger context windows. You can upload your contract rates or use the hosted default.
[02:28] Tom: So the console will show daily and cumulative cost by route, and I can export?
[02:32] Ethan: Yup, export CSV, and there's a per-day drilldown. Also our Cost Insights tab will show anomalies and recommend batching or a quantization profile if we detect high unit costs.
[02:45] Sarah: How accurate are those recommendations? We need to avoid degrading quality for certain routes.
[02:51] Ethan: Recommendations are heuristic initially — we run lightweight simulations using your token distributions. For anything we suggest, we'd run a small A/B against your eval prompts to measure quality delta. We can guard with rollout policies.
[03:06] [03:06] Jorge: Can we set per-route budgets and enforcement? For example stop all non-critical routes when monthly budget hits 90%?
[03:14] Priya (joined): Priya here — yeah you can configure per-route quotas and automatic actions: soft alert, hard throttle, or fallback to a cheaper model variant.
[03:25] Leah: Is that enforced in the control plane or do we need to implement client side?
[03:29] Priya: It's enforced server-side; you set policies in the console, and the routing layer applies them. For strict environment constraints we also support tagging requests for customer-side routing.
[03:40] Tom: And audit logs? I need to know who changed policies.
[03:44] Ethan: There's an audit log export. We capture config changes, who made them, and timestamps. Also integrates with KMS for key operations if you're on Private.
[03:54] Sarah: Data residency — our data must stay in eu-central. Does the console show region mapping and where inference ran?
[03:59] Ethan: Yes, per-request metadata includes region of execution. On Private/VPC you control region; on Hosted we can pin tenants to specific regions. We'll add the region column to your exports.
[04:12] Jorge: Ok, can you demo a scenario where a route suddenly spikes and how we'd triage in the console?
[04:17] Ethan: Sure — I'll trigger the Alerts tab. So here's a typical incident view: spike in requests for route "assistant-chat-prod". You can open the route timeline, see percentiles, top prompt patterns, and the top downstream users. Also there are token-level heatmaps.
[04:35] [04:35] Ethan: You can then click to open a quick action: throttle to 50%, switch to a cheaper model variant, or start a bulk export of recent requests for analysis.
[04:45] Sarah: How is the "cheaper model variant" determined? Do you maintain model compatibility?
[04:52] Ethan: We have verified variant pairs — e.g., 13B quantized vs 70B FP32 — and the system maps fallbacks based on architecture compatibility. You can edit mappings.
[05:05] Tom: For billing alignment we need line-item granularity across teams and cost centers. Can the console tag routes to cost centers?
[05:12] Ethan: Yes — you can add tags to routes and then create cost reports grouped by tags, route, model, or customer team. We can push to S3 or BigQuery for your internal FinOps pipeline.
[05:25] Jorge: There's a lot here, what's the onboarding time for mapping our existing infra?
[05:30] Maya: Typically 1-2 weeks to spin up a pilot integration plus a couple days to connect billing exports for visibility. For Dedicated/private it can be slightly longer.
[05:39] Sarah: We want a pilot that mirrors our peak traffic shape. Are you able to run trace-based replay?
[05:46] Ethan: Yes — our test harness can replay traces against the runtime to produce expected cost and latency profiles. We'll need a sanitized trace from you; we can run it in a staging project.
[06:00] Leah: Security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC, encryption at rest, KMS, SOC2. Any gaps for us?
[06:07] Priya: We support SSO/SAML, fine-grained RBAC, per-route access controls, and integration with your KMS. We are SOC 2 compliant; I'll drop the security pack after the call.
[06:18] Tom: About the cost numbers — can you walk through a simple worked example for a route where we do 100k requests/day, avg input 400 tokens, output 800 tokens on model X?
[06:30] Ethan: Sure, using the pricing profile uploaded here: at $0.00002 per input token and $0.00006 per output token the daily cost is (100k * 400 * .00002) + (100k * 800 * .00006) = input 800, output 4,800 so daily ~ $5,600, roughly. The console will calculate this dynamically and show per-minute cost burn.
[07:00] [07:00] Sarah: That per-route view will be helpful. Also can we set alerts on unit-cost anomalies? Sometimes prompt engineering changes spike token lengths.
[07:08] Ethan: Yes — anomaly detection triggers for sudden changes in avg tokens per request or unit cost, and you can set automated rollback to a pinned prompt set.
[07:18] Jorge: Any integration with our existing pager duty / slack?
[07:22] Ethan: Full integration — alerts to Slack, PagerDuty escalation, and webhook sinks.
[07:28] Leah: Latency SLOs — can we configure percentiles and get SLO burn-down dashboards?
[07:33] Priya: You can set SLOs per route and track error budget consumption; we also surface tokenizer-level hotspots that cause long decoding times.
[07:45] Tom: From a billing perspective, will you provide estimated monthly run-rate if we scale to 10M requests/day?
[07:51] Ethan: We can run scale projections in the Cost Insights tab. For large scale we usually recommend Dedicated reserved capacity to stabilize unit cost.
[08:02] Sarah: Ok let's talk pilot scope. We want to test: 1) per-route billing/export, 2) latency SLOs on 95/99 pctl, 3) fallback mapping, and 4) security docs.
[08:12] Maya: Sounds good. Proposed pilot: 2-week pilot in staging, Redwood provides replay harness + config, Velosys provides sanitized trace and decision criteria.
[08:20] Jorge: That's acceptable. Who's responsible for setting the routes?
[08:24] Maya: We'll provide a mapping template — Ethan will help onboard and Priya will help with RBAC and security settings.
[08:30] Tom: Can we get a sample of the per-route export CSV? I want header names so finance can map fields.
[08:36] Ethan: I'll attach the sample csv in the follow-up email. It includes columns: date, route_name, model, region, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_input, cost_output, total_cost, latency_p50, p90, p99, tags.
[08:50] [08:50] Priya: Another note — if you opt for Dedicated we can surface GPU-level utilization metrics as well.
[08:57] Sarah: Any obvious red flags from your side about our requests pattern?
[09:01] Ethan: From what Tom shared earlier, you have long outputs which dominate cost; we might experiment with structured responses and post-processing to reduce token count for some routes. But we'll A/B first.
[09:12] Jorge: Ok good.
[09:15] Maya: Quick recap of next steps: Maya will send pricing + per-route spreadsheet, Ethan will share pilot config + sample CSV, Priya will share SOC2/security pack, Tom will send sanitized trace and token volumes. We'll schedule the pilot kickoff for the week of 3/16.
[09:33] Sarah: Sounds good, thanks.
[09:36] Jorge: Thanks all.
[09:38] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up.
